label: Raw Resources
note: Substances pulled straight out of the world: mined, harvested, shot off asteroids or looted from sentinels.

label: Refined and Crafted Materials
note: Refiner outputs and crafted intermediates. Not sold and not consumed: they exist to feed blueprints.

label: Trade Goods
note: Bought low, sold high. No use beyond the trade terminal, so it wants its own container.

label: Food and Ingredients
note: Anything the Nutrient Processor accepts or produces, plus the baits cooked from it.

label: Fish
note: The fishing catalogue. High churn, its own economy, never wanted next to anything else.

label: Technology and Upgrade Modules
note: Installable technology plus the C, B and A grade modules that slot beside it. The working stock.

label: S-Class and Illegal Modules
note: S-Class, Illegal and Forbidden rolls, and their Supreme/Banned packaged equivalents. Hoarded, compared roll by roll, never spent casually.

label: Utility Consumables
note: One-shot supplies: fuel, ammo, charge packs and deployable field gear.

label: Curiosities and Artifacts
note: Story loot, alien relics, procedural dig finds and one-off quest tokens. Hoardable, unusable, best quarantined.

label: Expedition and Seasonal Rewards
note: Claimable exclusive starships, multi-tools and companion eggs earned outside normal play.

label: Base Building: Structure
note: Load-bearing base parts, terminals, farming and power: what a base is actually made of.

label: Base Building: Decoration
note: Purely visual base parts, fossils, posters and fireworks. Enormous, and never needed mid-flight.

label: Ship and Freighter Construction
note: Corvette hull sets, freighter modules and Starship Fabricator components: vehicle building, not base building.

label: Cosmetics and Appearance
note: Exosuit and ship looks, emotes and companion genetics. Cosmetic only, claim once, never restock.

label: Salvage and Junk
note: Derelict gunk, flotsam, class-rated salvage and Rusted module rolls. Vendor fodder that clogs a working inventory.

label: Packed Technology
note: Matched by SHAPE, not by id: an id carrying a #hash whose stem no table names. An uninstalled module sits in an inventory as a Product capped at 1 with a procedural hash, and the game generates ids for these that appear in no shipped table. Every other bucket is a lookup; this one is the rule that catches what a lookup cannot.

label: System and Non-Inventory
note: Never occupies a storage slot: currencies, reputation deltas, settlement stat tokens, world-object repair sockets, cooking category placeholders.

label: Corvette Parts
note: Corvette hull sections, bridges, engines, wings and interior fittings: the parts a Corvette is assembled from. Matched on the game's own display name or subtitle containing "Corvette", not on the CV_ id prefix -- the 31 procedural CV_* entries are upgrade modules that install into a Corvette, and they stay in Technology and Upgrade Modules. Split out of Ship and Freighter Construction because a Corvette build fills a container on its own and buried the freighter parts next to it.
